context.process_name: Distribution Economics: Waterfall, Tax Withholding & Notices
context.objective: Document how we carry out Distribution Economics: Waterfall, Tax Withholding & Notices, the controls and what needs confirmation.

turns.text: What starts this work?

It starts when cash proceeds are received or expected, when a deal closes or a realization happens, or when the client asks us to calculate or carry out a distribution. It is event-driven, there is no fixed calendar for it.

The first step is mine as the event preparer on the capital activity team or the Fund Team. I take the client instructions and the bank records and confirm the entity, the deal, the amount, whether the cash is only expected or has actually been received, and the requested payment date. I work out whether it is a distribution-only event or a combined call-and-distribution event, which we call a net event. Then I assign a second reviewer, list what we will need from the client's tax team, and link the work to the controlling FA-01 event calendar. All of that goes into the event brief and the capital activity workbook.

There is one branch at this point. If the cash has come in and I know which deal it belongs to, I carry on to classifying the proceeds. If cash has come in without deal context, or the client's instructions conflict with each other, I escalate and the client has to identify and classify it in writing before I model anything, and I keep that written confirmation with the bank support.
Once the deal is identified, what do you use to determine how the proceeds are classified?

I use the client's deal information, the bank activity and the closing support. That is the second step, identifying and classifying the proceeds, and I do it as the event preparer.

First I confirm whether the amount is expected cash or cash that has actually cleared the bank. I match the cash to the right portfolio company, deal, fund and bank account. Then I classify each component as return of capital, realized gain, dividend or income, or another supported category, and I flag any asset conversion, escrow, holdback or other piece that changes the distribution economics. It all goes into the proceeds-input tab of the workbook, with the bank support and the client correspondence kept alongside. My check before moving on is that the total classified proceeds equal the amount being modeled and that every component has support behind it.

The branch here is about whether the support is enough. If it is, I move on to updating the cumulative proceeds. If the bank activity on its own does not tell me the deal or the character of the money, I stop the calculations and get a written classification from the client. I never decide the deal, tax or GAAP classification from the bank description alone.
How do you update the cumulative proceeds after the classified proceeds pass your check?

I start with the prior approved cumulative proceeds working file and add the current proceeds to it by their supported classification. Then I confirm the prior distributions, the remaining invested capital and the cumulative contributions.

After that I reconcile the starting balance and the current balance to the prior event, the general ledger, the trial balance, the bank records and the partner-capital records. For the historical balances I pull the system power report, the trial balance and the partner-capital files. I do the work as the preparer and the second reviewer verifies it.

The branch is on the reconciliation. If every difference is resolved or documented, I have a reconciled waterfall starting point and I go on to confirming the waterfall rules for the fund. If the starting point has a difference I cannot explain, the waterfall calculation is paused and does not start until that difference is cleared.
How do you confirm the waterfall rules for the fund before calculating the distribution?

I work from the LPA, the side letters, the approved waterfall model, how it was treated before and the facts of the current event. I do this step together with the second reviewer and with input from the client.

I write down the exact order and definitions for return of capital, preferred return, catch-up, carried interest, the residual split and any holdback or clawback provision. I confirm whether the calculation applies to the whole fund, to each deal, to each tranche or to some other defined segment, and I confirm any escrow or holdback treatment. That is all recorded in the waterfall methodology record and the model.

The branch is whether the rules are clear. If the rule set is traceable to the governing documents and has been independently reviewed, I lock the rule set for this event and move on to running the cash waterfall. If a treatment has changed or a rule in the LPA is ambiguous, I record it, pause, and get written direction from the client or the legal adviser. We do not make up a missing rule ourselves. Once the written interpretation comes back, the rule set is locked and the work carries on.
How do you apply the locked rule set in the cash waterfall calculation?

I enter the current proceeds into the controlled model, which is the capital activity waterfall model, and apply the fund's return of capital, preferred return, catch-up, carried interest and residual calculations in the approved order. From that I calculate the limited partner and general partner allocations, including any holdback.

Then I check it. Allocated cash plus retained or held cash has to equal the total modeled proceeds, and the result has to agree with the locked rules. What comes out is the draft cash waterfall result.

The branch in this step is the carry position. If the model shows the fund is in a carry position, the cash carry the waterfall allows is included in the result. If the fund is not in a carry position, no cash carry is paid. I document what the model shows and the reviewer confirms it. Either way I then move on to the tax side.

One more thing that can happen here: if the waterfall gives a negative, residual or otherwise unexpected result, I investigate it, and where the economics are unclear I get confirmation from the client or legal before going further.
What do you do first on the tax side after the cash waterfall result is ready?

The first thing is getting the taxable-income allocation for the event from the client's tax team or their tax adviser. They provide or approve the tax conclusions, and I only add them into the calculation. I confirm that the taxable income may differ from the cash, and I look at whether the GP or another investor is receiving taxable income without the corresponding cash.

That is where the branch is. If there is taxable income without cash carry, the client's tax adviser or the client decides whether a tax distribution is permitted or required. If the governing documents permit it, I calculate or add the tax distribution needed to cover the tax liability, in a dedicated section of the workbook, and I keep its support separate from the cash waterfall support. If it is not permitted, there is no tax distribution and I just carry the approved taxable-income allocation forward. Either way I get the tax team's or client's approval of the tax inputs and the output before I go on to withholding.

The other thing that can happen is that the required tax input is missing or conflicting. In that case the final economics are held until it is sorted out. We never replace the approved tax conclusion with one we worked out ourselves.
How do you determine and apply withholding once the tax inputs and output are approved?

I work from the client's or tax team's withholding schedule and their direction, in the capital activity workbook. I identify every investor who is subject to withholding and the jurisdiction and rate that applies to them. Then I either apply the approved rate to the approved taxable-income base, or I bring in the approved client schedule as it stands. Any approved prior-period true-ups or supplemental adjustments go in separately. For each investor I calculate the gross distribution, the withholding and the net cash.

The check is that gross minus withholding equals net cash for every investor, and that the schedule totals reconcile to the model and to the approved tax input. The second reviewer checks the result.

There are two branches in this step. The first is the type of event. If it is distribution-only, there is no netting and the net cash is simply gross less withholding. If it is a net event, I include the approved withholding in the call-and-distribution net calculation, but I keep separate support for each component before netting, and the reviewer or the client confirms the netting.

The second is the schedule itself. If the withholding input is in and approved, I carry on to the investor allocations. If it is late or gets revised, or a rate, a jurisdiction or an investor classification is missing, I escalate to the client or the tax adviser, and the affected calculations, notices and payments are held or recalculated until we have the new version of the schedule and a renewed approval.
How do you turn the approved investor-level amounts into distribution notices?

Not straight away, there are a few steps before the notices. The amounts are not approved yet at this point. Notices are only produced after the internal review and after the client has approved the economics and we have locked the version. The step that comes right after withholding is applying the investor allocation rules, and that one is mine as the preparer.

I confirm the allocation basis the governing terms require, which can be the commitment percentage, the limited partner percentage, a deal-specific basis or another basis. I use the approved investor list and any approved special allocations. Then, in the allocation engine of the capital activity workbook, I calculate each investor's proceeds components, the carry and tax effects, the withholding and the net cash, and I reconcile the investor-level totals back to the fund-level waterfall and the tax schedules. Last, I populate the final summary tab, which is what the notices and the payment support are later built from. The result is the draft investor-level distribution schedule.

The branch is the reconciliation. If the investor totals equal the approved fund-level components, subject only to documented rounding, the package goes to the second reviewer for the internal review. If there is an allocation difference I cannot explain, or a percentage that is not supported by the governing method, I pause there until it is resolved. Percentages sitting in Excel are not treated as authoritative on their own.
What does the second reviewer check in the draft investor-level distribution schedule?

The second reviewer looks at more than the schedule. They get the whole package: the proceeds, waterfall, tax, withholding, allocation and notice-support working files, plus the draft notices.

They check the proceeds amount and classification and that the roll-forward is continuous from the prior event. They check the waterfall rules and formulas, the carried interest, the preferred return, the tax distribution and any holdback. They check the taxable-income and withholding inputs against the approved schedules. They check the investor totals, the gross, withholding and net calculations and the reconciliations. And on the draft notices they check the component labels, the GAAP and tax breakdowns and the footnotes. Their review comments are recorded and each one has to be resolved.

The branch is the outcome of that review. If everything is cleared, the second reviewer signs off, and that sign-off has to be in place before anything goes to the client. That gives us the internally cleared distribution package, and the next step is sending it to the client for approval. If there are unresolved errors or gaps in the source information, they come back to me as preparer, or go to the client or the tax adviser if it is their input, and the process stops there until they are fixed and the reviewer has cleared them.
After the internally cleared package is sent to the client, what happens before the economics are approved and the version is locked?

When I send the package I point out to the client every tax input that is still estimated, pending or late, so they know what might move. I coordinate this step and the client is the one who approves.

The branch is what the client comes back with. If they are happy with it as it stands, I get their final written approval, and then I lock and retain that version. The locked version is the one used for the notices, the posting and the payment. If they come back with changes, for example to timing, the character of the proceeds, tax amounts, withholding or the notice language, I incorporate the approved changes, recalculate the affected amounts, and repeat the reconciliations and the review checks. Then it goes back for the final written approval and I lock it. Nothing is released or paid from an unapproved version. The client's written approval has to be on file before any entry is recorded or any payment is made.

There are two exceptions around this step. If a change arrives after an entry has already been recorded or a payment made, we follow the controlled correction process and get renewed approval. And if a bank holiday or a cut-off time threatens the wires, the client and Treasury decide between changing the timing or agreeing an approved alternative execution plan, and we keep the revised calendar and the approval.
Once the version is locked, how are distribution notices produced?

They are produced from the locked approved investor schedule. I merge the investor data into the controlled Word notice template with a mail merge, and the notices come out as PDFs. Each notice discloses the gross proceeds, the components, the transaction type, taxable income, withholding, the net payment and any footnotes that apply. Then the second reviewer and I reconcile every notice back to the locked investor schedule and complete the QA.

In the same step I hand the approved posting and payment support over to the Fund Team and Treasury. From there it is executed through FA-01 and FA-17. Bank holidays and cut-off times are checked, the Fund Team records the general ledger entry, Treasury sends the wires, and Investor Services publishes the notices on the investor portal.

The branch is whether everything ties. If the notice and payment totals agree to the locked schedule and all the FA-01 and FA-17 gates are complete, the payment and the release go ahead. If there is a notice mismatch, a bank closure, invalid instructions or an incomplete approval, the payment or the release is held. Investor Services hold the release when a notice does not match the approved investor list, and Treasury holds payments when approvals, instructions or funding are incomplete or a holiday or cut-off gets in the way.
What confirms that the distribution is fully completed after the posting, wires and notice release?

There is one last step after the money goes out, and it is done by the assigned Fund Team or by me as the event preparer. I track the amounts withheld for tax separately from the investor net payments, and I give the supporting records to whoever is responsible for paying the tax authority. I update the investor capital accounts and the historical contribution and distribution records, and I update the cumulative proceeds history and the carried-interest tracking. Then I reconcile the actual wires, the withholding held or remitted, the general ledger balances and the locked schedule. I also complete any client-specific uploads or open-template reporting. For One Rock, for example, the Cobalt upload has to be completed within two days of the event.

What confirms it is finished is that final reconciliation. Gross distribution has to equal net investor cash plus withholding, and the actual cash and the accounting have to agree to the locked event with no unexplained difference.

The branch is on that check. If it all reconciles, the event is closed out and we keep the reconciled post-distribution record and the remittance support. If there is unremitted withholding, a rejected wire or an accounting difference, I escalate it immediately and the closeout stays open. An unexplained difference prevents closeout and may need a correction or a reposting.

One thing I cannot tell you is who actually owns remitting the withholding to the tax authority. I do not know that, and I do not know the payment steps, the due dates or what counts as proof of remittance either. The tax process expert would be the person to confirm it. What I do know is that if the remittance owner is unclear on an event, the responsible role has to be assigned before closeout.
What are the practical consequences if a distribution is delayed or processed incorrectly?
This capture still has open sections. 15 of 16 are open; the Notes list shows which. You can create a partial draft.

notes.summary: After payment, the Fund Team or preparer performs closeout updates and reconciliation. Unremitted withholding, rejected wires or accounting differences keep closeout open. The participant does not know who remits withholding or the remittance procedure; One Rock requires a Cobalt upload within two days.

topics.answer: Distribution Economics: Waterfall, Tax Withholding & Notices
The work calculates and carries out distribution economics, producing approved investor amounts and notices and supporting posting and payment.

Work starts when cash proceeds are received or expected, a deal closes or a realization happens, or the client asks for a distribution calculation or execution. The work is event-driven, with no fixed calendar.

The withholding-remittance owner, payment steps, due dates and proof of remittance remain unknown to the participant; the tax process expert could confirm them.
The reported downstream outcomes are a general ledger entry recorded by the Fund Team, wires sent by Treasury and notices published by Investor Services; release and payment are subject to schedule tie-outs and FA-01 and FA-17 gates.
Final reconciliation confirms completion: gross distribution equals net investor cash plus withholding, and actual cash and accounting agree to the locked event without unexplained differences. Reconciled events are closed out; unremitted withholding, rejected wires or accounting differences keep closeout open.

The participant is the event preparer on the capital activity team or Fund Team and performs the first intake and proceeds-classification steps.
The role accountable for the overall result has not been established.
The participant does not know who owns withholding remittance; the tax process expert could confirm it. An unclear event-level remittance owner must be assigned before closeout.

At the first step, the event preparer takes client instructions and bank records and confirms the entity, deal, amount, whether cash is expected or received, and requested payment date; determines whether the event is distribution-only or a combined call-and-distribution net event; assigns a second reviewer; lists needs from the client's tax team; links the work to the controlling FA-01 event calendar; and puts the information in the event brief and capital activity workbook.
If cash has been received and the preparer knows which deal it belongs to, the preparer proceeds to classify the proceeds. If cash has been received without deal context, or client instructions conflict, the preparer escalates; modeling waits until the client identifies and classifies the proceeds in writing, and that confirmation is kept with bank support.
For the second step, the event preparer uses client deal information, bank activity and closing support, confirms expected versus cleared cash, and matches it to the portfolio company, deal, fund and bank account.
The preparer classifies each proceeds component as return of capital, realized gain, dividend or income, or another supported category, and flags asset conversions, escrows, holdbacks or other pieces that change distribution economics. The preparer records this in the workbook's proceeds-input tab and keeps bank support and client correspondence alongside.
If support is sufficient, the preparer moves on to updating cumulative proceeds. If bank activity alone does not establish the deal or character of the money, the preparer stops calculations and obtains written client classification.
The preparer starts with the prior approved cumulative proceeds working file, adds current proceeds by supported classification, and confirms prior distributions, remaining invested capital and cumulative contributions.
The preparer reconciles starting and current balances to the prior event, general ledger, trial balance, bank records and partner-capital records; the second reviewer verifies the work. If all differences are resolved or documented, the preparer proceeds to confirm fund waterfall rules. An unexplained starting-point difference pauses the waterfall calculation until cleared.
The preparer and second reviewer, with client input, confirm waterfall rules using the LPA, side letters, approved waterfall model, prior treatment and current event facts. The preparer records tier order and definitions, calculation scope, and escrow or holdback treatment in the waterfall methodology record and model.
When the rules are traceable to governing documents and independently reviewed, the preparer locks the event rule set and runs the cash waterfall. For changed treatment or an ambiguous LPA rule, the preparer records the issue and pauses for written client or legal-adviser direction; once received, the rule set is locked and work continues.
The preparer enters current proceeds into the controlled capital activity waterfall model and applies return of capital, preferred return, catch-up, carried interest and residual calculations in the approved order. The resulting draft cash waterfall includes limited partner and general partner allocations and any holdback.
If the model shows a carry position, the draft includes the cash carry allowed by the waterfall; otherwise no cash carry is paid. The preparer documents the model's result, the reviewer confirms it, and the work moves to tax.
The preparer investigates negative, residual or otherwise unexpected waterfall results. Where the economics are unclear, the preparer obtains client or legal confirmation before proceeding.
After the draft cash waterfall, the preparer obtains the event's taxable-income allocation from the client's tax team or tax adviser, adds their provided or approved tax conclusions to the calculation, and checks whether taxable income differs from cash and whether the GP or another investor receives taxable income without corresponding cash.
If taxable income arises without cash carry, the client's tax adviser or client decides whether a tax distribution is permitted or required. If governing documents permit it, the preparer calculates or adds the tax distribution needed to cover the tax liability in a dedicated workbook section, keeping its support separate from cash waterfall support; otherwise the preparer carries the approved taxable-income allocation forward without a tax distribution.
The preparer uses the client's or tax team's withholding schedule and direction in the capital activity workbook to identify each affected investor, jurisdiction and rate. The preparer applies the approved rate to the approved taxable-income base or imports the approved client schedule as provided, records approved prior-period true-ups or supplemental adjustments separately, and calculates gross distribution, withholding and net cash for each investor.
For a distribution-only event, the preparer does not net: net cash is gross less withholding. For a net event, the preparer includes approved withholding in the call-and-distribution net calculation, keeps separate support for each component before netting, and obtains reviewer or client confirmation of the netting.
Once the withholding input is received and approved, the preparer proceeds to investor allocations. If the schedule is late or revised, or a rate, jurisdiction or investor classification is missing, the preparer escalates to the client or tax adviser; affected calculations, notices and payments are held or recalculated until a new schedule and renewed approval are obtained.
After withholding, the preparer confirms the governing allocation basis, uses the approved investor list and special allocations, and calculates investor proceeds components, carry and tax effects, withholding and net cash in the workbook allocation engine. The preparer reconciles investor totals to the fund waterfall and tax schedules and populates the final summary tab, producing a draft investor-level distribution schedule.
If investor totals equal approved fund-level components subject only to documented rounding, the package goes to the second reviewer for internal review. An unexplained allocation difference or percentage unsupported by the governing method pauses the work until resolved.
Draft notices are included in the internal review package. Notice production follows internal review, client economics approval and version locking; the final summary tab later supports notices and payments.
The second reviewer receives the full working package and draft notices. Review comments are recorded and must be resolved; unresolved errors or source gaps return to the preparer or to the client or tax adviser for their inputs, and work stops until fixed and cleared. Once everything is cleared, the reviewer signs off before the internally cleared package goes to the client for approval.
The distinction between draft notices reviewed internally and notice production after approval and version locking remains unclear.
The preparer coordinates client approval and flags estimated, pending or late tax inputs when sending the package. If the client accepts it, the preparer obtains final written approval, then locks and retains the version used for notices, posting and payment.
If the client requests changes, the preparer incorporates approved changes, recalculates affected amounts and repeats reconciliations and review checks. The package returns for final written approval before the preparer locks it.
For a change after an entry has been recorded or payment made, the team follows the controlled correction process and obtains renewed approval.
If a bank holiday or cut-off threatens wires, the client and Treasury decide whether to change timing or agree an approved alternative execution plan; the revised calendar and approval are kept.
From the locked approved investor schedule, the preparer mail-merges investor data into the controlled Word notice template to produce PDFs. The notices disclose gross proceeds, components, transaction type, taxable income, withholding, net payment and applicable footnotes; the preparer and second reviewer reconcile each notice to the locked schedule and complete QA.
The preparer hands approved posting and payment support to the Fund Team and Treasury for execution through FA-01 and FA-17. Bank holidays and cut-offs are checked; the Fund Team records the general ledger entry, Treasury sends wires and Investor Services publishes notices on the investor portal.
Payment and release proceed when notice and payment totals agree to the locked schedule and all FA-01 and FA-17 gates are complete. Investor Services holds release for a notice mismatch with the approved investor list; Treasury holds payments for incomplete approvals, instructions or funding, or a holiday or cut-off obstruction.
After money goes out, the assigned Fund Team or event preparer performs the last step. The participant tracks tax withholding separately from investor net payments, gives supporting records to the person responsible for paying the tax authority, and updates investor capital accounts, contribution and distribution history, cumulative proceeds history and carry tracking.
The participant reconciles actual wires, withholding held or remitted, general ledger balances and the locked schedule, and completes client-specific uploads or open-template reporting. If reconciled, the event closes; unremitted withholding, a rejected wire or an accounting difference is escalated and closeout stays open. An unexplained difference may require correction or reposting.

The event preparer confirms entity, deal, amount, cash status and requested payment date using client instructions and bank records, determines the event type and assigns a second reviewer.
The second reviewer's comments on the full package are recorded and must be resolved; the reviewer signs off after everything is cleared, before the package goes to the client.
Before moving on, the preparer checks that classified proceeds total the amount modeled and that every component has supporting evidence.
The preparer reconciles starting and current cumulative proceeds balances against the prior event, general ledger, trial balance, bank records and partner-capital records; the second reviewer verifies the work. Differences must be resolved or documented, and an unexplained starting-point difference blocks the waterfall calculation until cleared.
The waterfall rule set must be traceable to governing documents and independently reviewed before it is locked for the event. Changed treatment or LPA ambiguity pauses the work pending written direction.
The preparer checks that allocated cash plus retained or held cash equals modeled proceeds and that the result agrees with the locked rules. The reviewer confirms the documented carry position.
Before proceeding to withholding, the preparer obtains the tax team's or client's approval of the tax inputs and output. Missing or conflicting required tax input holds final economics until resolved; the team does not substitute its own conclusion for the approved tax conclusion.
The preparer checks that gross less withholding equals net cash for each investor and that schedule totals reconcile to the model and approved tax input; the second reviewer checks the result. The reviewer or client confirms netting for a net event.
The preparer reconciles investor totals to fund-level waterfall components and tax schedules; only documented rounding differences are allowed before the package goes to the second reviewer. Unsupported percentages or unexplained differences halt progress until resolved.
How a delayed client economics approval is pursued or escalated remains unspecified; Treasury holds payment when approvals are incomplete.
The second reviewer checks proceeds amount and classification, roll-forward continuity, waterfall rules and formulas, carry, preferred return, tax distribution and holdbacks. They compare taxable-income and withholding inputs with approved schedules, check investor calculations and reconciliations, and review draft notice labels, GAAP and tax breakdowns and footnotes.
The client gives final written economics approval. No release or payment may use an unapproved version, and written approval must be on file before any entry is recorded or payment made.
The preparer and second reviewer reconcile every notice to the locked investor schedule and complete QA. Payment and release require notice and payment totals to agree to that schedule and all FA-01 and FA-17 gates to be complete.
At closeout the participant reconciles actual wires, withholding held or remitted and general ledger balances against the locked schedule. Unremitted withholding, rejected wires and accounting differences are escalated immediately.

The intake route changes with the available context: known deal context permits classification, while received cash without deal context or conflicting client instructions prompts escalation and written client identification and classification before modeling.
Other client-, fund- or system-specific differences, and the effort, charging and removal constraints for the One Rock reporting requirement, remain unestablished.
When bank activity alone does not establish the deal or the money's character, the preparer stops calculations and obtains written client classification; sufficiently supported proceeds move on to cumulative-proceeds updating.
Waterfall calculation scope depends on the confirmed rule: it can apply to the whole fund, each deal, each tranche or another defined segment. Changed treatment or LPA ambiguity adds a pause for written interpretation before the rule set is locked.
The cash waterfall output differs by carry position: an allowed cash carry is included when the fund is in carry; otherwise no cash carry is paid.
For taxable income without cash carry, the tax-distribution route depends on governing-document permission: a permitted distribution is calculated or added, while an unpermitted one is omitted and the approved allocation carried forward.
Event type changes withholding treatment: distribution-only events have no netting, while combined call-and-distribution events include approved withholding in the net calculation, retain component support separately and require reviewer or client confirmation.
Depending on the approved input, the preparer either applies an approved withholding rate to the approved taxable-income base or brings in the approved client schedule as provided.
Investor allocations use the basis required by the governing terms: commitment percentage, LP percentage, a deal-specific basis or another basis; approved special allocations are also used.
Client-requested changes to timing, proceeds character, tax, withholding or notice language require incorporation of approved changes, recalculation and repeated reconciliation and review before renewed submission for approval.
A notice mismatch with the approved investor list causes Investor Services to hold release; incomplete approvals, instructions or funding, or holiday and cut-off constraints, cause Treasury to hold payment.
Closeout includes client-specific uploads or open-template reporting. For One Rock, the Cobalt upload must be completed within two days of the event.

The process consumes the event taxable-income allocation from the client's tax team or tax adviser, and requires tax-team or client approval of the tax inputs and output before withholding.
Requires approval from Client's tax team or client: Tax inputs and output before withholding.
The process consumes the client's or tax team's withholding schedule and direction. The preparer escalates late or revised schedules and missing investor withholding details to the client or tax adviser; affected work waits for a new schedule and renewed approval.
Uses the output of Client or tax team: Withholding schedule and direction used for investor withholding.
The process requires client approval of the economics before notices are produced, after internal review and with the version locked.
The process requires the client's final written economics approval before the preparer locks the version; that approval must be on file before entries or payments.
When a bank holiday or cut-off threatens wires, the client and Treasury decide on changed timing or an approved alternative execution plan.
The preparer hands approved posting and payment support to the Fund Team and Treasury, with execution through FA-01 and FA-17. The Fund Team records the entry, Treasury sends wires and Investor Services publishes notices.
The participant hands withholding supporting records to whoever is responsible for paying the tax authority; the remittance owner and payment procedure are unknown to the participant.
Hands off to Withholding remittance responsible party: The participant provides supporting records to whoever is responsible for paying the tax authority; the owner is unknown.

The event brief and capital activity workbook record the first-step information; the workbook's proceeds-input tab records the proceeds classification.
Ownership and implementation of workbook logic, the system of record, and any re-entry elsewhere remain unidentified.
The preparer uses a prior approved cumulative proceeds working file and pulls a system power report, trial balance and partner-capital files for historical balances.
The approved waterfall model is an input to rule confirmation; the confirmed methodology is recorded in the model and the waterfall methodology record.
The preparer enters current proceeds into the controlled capital activity waterfall model to calculate the draft allocation result.
The preparer calculates or adds a permitted tax distribution in a dedicated workbook section.
The preparer works in the capital activity workbook on withholding, either applying approved rates to approved taxable-income bases or bringing in the approved client schedule.
The preparer calculates investor-level distribution components in the capital activity workbook's allocation engine and populates its final summary tab.
The preparer uses Word mail merge to create PDF notices from the locked investor schedule; Investor Services publishes them on the investor portal.
One Rock requires a Cobalt upload within two days of the event as part of client-specific reporting.
Normal event counts, peaks, exception frequency and effort per event have not been described.

map.title: Distribution Economics

steps.title: Distribution event arises
steps.description: Cash proceeds are received or expected, a deal closes or realization occurs, or the client requests a distribution calculation or execution.

steps.title: Confirm event details
steps.actor: Event preparer, capital activity team or Fund Team
steps.description: Use client instructions and bank records to confirm the entity, deal, amount, cash receipt status and requested payment date.

steps.title: Determine event type
steps.description: Determine whether the event is distribution-only or a combined call-and-distribution, called a net event.

steps.title: Set up event brief
steps.system: Event brief, capital activity workbook and FA-01 event calendar
steps.description: Assign a second reviewer, list what is needed from the client's tax team and link the work to the controlling FA-01 event calendar. Record the event information in the event brief and capital activity workbook.

steps.title: Is context sufficient?
steps.description: Consider whether received cash has known deal context and whether client instructions conflict. The route for expected cash without conflicting instructions is UNKNOWN.

steps.title: Identify and classify proceeds
steps.description: Confirm whether cash is expected or has cleared, and match it to the portfolio company, deal, fund and bank account. Classify components and flag asset conversions, escrows, holdbacks or other items affecting distribution economics. Record the information in the proceeds-input tab and keep bank support and client correspondence alongside.

steps.title: Escalate unclear event
steps.description: Escalate received cash without deal context or conflicting client instructions. The escalation recipient is UNKNOWN.

steps.title: Provide written client classification
steps.description: The client identifies and classifies the item in writing. This written confirmation is required before modeling in the escalated case.

steps.title: Retain written confirmation
steps.description: Keep the client's written confirmation with the bank support.

steps.title: Model the event
steps.description: Modeling is reported as later work. In the escalated case, written client identification and classification are required first; modeling details and its other prerequisites are UNKNOWN.

steps.title: Do proceeds and support reconcile?
steps.description: Check that total classified proceeds equal the amount being modeled and that every component has support. Bank activity alone may not establish the deal or character of the money.

steps.title: Obtain written client classification
steps.description: Stop calculations and obtain a written classification from the client when bank activity alone does not establish the deal or character of the money.

steps.title: Update cumulative proceeds
steps.description: Start with the prior approved cumulative proceeds working file and add current proceeds by supported classification.

steps.title: Confirm historical balances
steps.description: Confirm prior distributions, remaining invested capital and cumulative contributions.

steps.title: Reconcile cumulative balances
steps.system: System power report, trial balance and partner-capital files
steps.description: Reconcile starting and current balances to the prior event, general ledger, trial balance, bank records and partner-capital records. Pull the system power report, trial balance and partner-capital files for historical balances.

steps.title: Verify cumulative proceeds work
steps.description: Verify the preparer's cumulative proceeds and reconciliation work. The detailed review checks and timing relative to advancement are UNKNOWN.

steps.title: Are reconciliation differences addressed?
steps.description: Determine whether every difference is resolved or documented, or whether the starting point has an unexplained difference.

steps.title: Wait for difference clearance
steps.description: Pause the waterfall calculation when a starting-point difference cannot be explained. The calculation cannot start until the difference is cleared.

steps.title: Confirm fund waterfall rules
steps.actor: Event preparer and second reviewer, with client input
steps.description: Use the LPA, side letters, approved model, prior treatment and current event facts to document the waterfall order and definitions. Confirm the calculation segment and escrow or holdback treatment.

steps.title: Are waterfall rules clear?
steps.description: Determine whether the rule set is traceable to governing documents and independently reviewed, or whether a changed treatment or ambiguous LPA rule requires written direction.

steps.title: Record issue and seek direction
steps.description: Record the changed treatment or ambiguous rule and seek written direction from the client or legal adviser. The work is paused; the team does not invent a missing rule.

steps.title: Wait for written interpretation
steps.description: Pause pending written interpretation from the client or legal adviser.

steps.title: Lock event rule set
steps.description: Lock the rule set for the event after the reported clear-rule checks or after written interpretation is received.

steps.title: Run cash waterfall
steps.description: Enter current proceeds into the controlled model and apply the fund's return of capital, preferred return, catch-up, carried interest and residual calculations in the approved order. Calculate limited partner and general partner allocations, including any holdback.

steps.title: Check waterfall result
steps.description: Check that allocated cash plus retained or held cash equals total modeled proceeds and that the result agrees with the locked rules.

steps.title: Is the fund in carry?
steps.description: Determine the carry position shown by the model. Include the cash carry allowed by the waterfall if the fund is in carry; otherwise no cash carry is paid.

steps.title: Document carry position
steps.description: Document what the model shows about the carry position.

steps.title: Confirm carry position
steps.description: Confirm what the model shows about the carry position. Detailed checks and retained review evidence are UNKNOWN.

steps.title: Investigate unexpected waterfall result
steps.description: Investigate a negative, residual or otherwise unexpected waterfall result. If the economics are unclear, obtain client or legal confirmation before going further.

steps.title: Obtain economics confirmation
steps.description: Obtain confirmation from the client or legal when the economics of an unexpected result are unclear, before going further.

steps.title: Obtain taxable-income allocation
steps.description: Obtain the event’s taxable-income allocation from the client’s tax team or tax adviser. They provide or approve the tax conclusions; the preparer does not substitute an independently determined conclusion.

steps.title: Add and assess tax allocation
steps.description: Add the tax conclusions into the calculation, confirm that taxable income may differ from cash, and look for taxable income allocated to the GP or another investor without corresponding cash.

steps.title: Is income without cash carry?
steps.description: Determine whether the reported taxable-income-without-cash-carry condition applies. The route when it does not apply is UNKNOWN.

steps.title: Decide tax distribution treatment
steps.description: Decide whether a tax distribution is permitted or required when taxable income arises without cash carry. The participant refers to permission under the governing documents; who interprets them and how the decision is recorded are UNKNOWN.

steps.title: Calculate or add tax distribution
steps.description: Calculate or add the tax distribution needed to cover the tax liability in a dedicated workbook section. Keep its support separate from the cash waterfall support.

steps.title: Carry tax allocation forward
steps.description: If a tax distribution is not permitted, carry the approved taxable-income allocation forward without a tax distribution.

steps.title: Approve tax inputs and output
steps.description: Approve the tax inputs and output before withholding. The approval mechanism, retained evidence and rejection handling are UNKNOWN.

steps.title: Identify withholding requirements
steps.description: Use the client’s or tax team’s withholding schedule and direction to identify each investor subject to withholding and the applicable jurisdiction and rate.

steps.title: Hold for tax input resolution
steps.description: Hold final economics when required tax input is missing or conflicting, until it is sorted out. The resolution process and resumption point are UNKNOWN.

steps.title: How is withholding applied?
steps.description: Use either the approved rate and taxable-income base or the approved client schedule as supplied.

steps.title: Apply approved withholding rate
steps.description: Apply the approved rate to the approved taxable-income base.

steps.title: Bring in approved schedule
steps.description: Bring in the approved client withholding schedule as it stands. The transfer method is UNKNOWN.

steps.title: Calculate investor withholding amounts
steps.description: Include approved prior-period true-ups or supplemental adjustments separately. Calculate gross distribution, withholding and net cash for each investor.

steps.title: Do withholding amounts reconcile?
steps.description: Check that gross less withholding equals net cash for each investor and that schedule totals reconcile to the model and approved tax input.

steps.title: Review withholding result
steps.description: Check the withholding result. The reviewer’s specific checks, evidence and failure handling are UNKNOWN.

steps.title: Is this a net event?
steps.description: Apply the event-type branch. Distribution-only events have no netting; net events include approved withholding in the call-and-distribution net calculation.

steps.title: Calculate net event
steps.description: Include approved withholding in the call-and-distribution net calculation and keep separate support for each component before netting.

steps.title: Confirm event netting
steps.description: Confirm the netting for a net event. The confirmation method and retained evidence are UNKNOWN.

steps.title: Is withholding input approved?
steps.description: Proceed to investor allocations when the withholding input is in and approved. Late or revised schedules and missing rates, jurisdictions or investor classifications require escalation and a hold or recalculation.

steps.title: Confirm investor allocation basis
steps.description: Confirm the basis required by the governing terms and use the approved investor list and any approved special allocations. The investor-level amounts are not yet approved.

steps.title: Escalate withholding input issues
steps.description: Escalate to the client or tax adviser when the schedule is late or revised, or a rate, jurisdiction or investor classification is missing. Hold or recalculate affected calculations, notices and payments until the new schedule version and renewed approval are available.

steps.title: Wait for schedule and approval
steps.description: Affected calculations, notices and payments remain held or subject to recalculation until both the new schedule version and renewed approval are available. Their order and the exact resumption point are UNKNOWN.

steps.title: Calculate and reconcile allocations
steps.description: Calculate each investor's proceeds components, carry and tax effects, withholding and net cash. Reconcile investor totals to the fund-level waterfall and tax schedules.

steps.title: Populate final summary tab
steps.description: Populate the final summary tab from the investor allocation work. Notices and payment support are later built from it.

steps.title: Do investor allocations reconcile?
steps.description: Determine whether investor totals equal the approved fund-level components subject only to documented rounding. An unexplained difference or a percentage unsupported by the governing method pauses the work.

steps.title: Review and clear package
steps.system: Working files and draft notices; review-comment location UNKNOWN
steps.description: The second reviewer checks the proceeds, roll-forward, waterfall, tax, withholding, allocations and draft notices. Comments are recorded and must be resolved; errors return to the preparer, or client or tax adviser for their input, before reviewer clearance and sign-off.

steps.title: Wait for allocation resolution
steps.description: Pause when an allocation difference cannot be explained or a percentage is unsupported by the governing method. The resolution method and resumption point are UNKNOWN.

steps.title: Coordinate client approval
steps.description: The preparer sends the internally cleared package to the client, identifies estimated, pending or late tax inputs, and coordinates approval. If the client requests changes, the preparer incorporates approved changes, recalculates affected amounts and repeats reconciliations and review checks before seeking final written approval.

steps.title: Lock economics version
steps.description: After final written client approval, lock and retain the approved version for notices, posting and payment. A change after an entry or payment follows the controlled correction process and requires renewed approval; if a bank holiday or cut-off threatens wires, the client and Treasury decide timing or an approved alternative execution plan, and the revised calendar and approval are kept.

steps.title: Produce notices and close event
steps.actor: Event preparer, second reviewer, Fund Team, Treasury and Investor Services
steps.system: Capital activity workbook, controlled Word template, FA-01, FA-17, investor portal and Cobalt for One Rock
steps.description: The preparer produces PDF notices from the locked schedule; the preparer and second reviewer reconcile them and complete QA, and the preparer hands approved support to the Fund Team and Treasury. The Fund Team records the entry, Treasury sends wires and Investor Services publishes notices, subject to the reported release gates and holds. After payment, the assigned Fund Team or preparer updates records, supplies tax-payment support, completes applicable reporting and reconciles the event for closeout; exceptions are escalated and closeout remains open.

steps.title: Distribution event arises
steps.description: Received or expected proceeds, a deal close or realization, or a client request starts the event. There is no fixed calendar.

steps.title: Prepare event brief
steps.actor: Event preparer on the capital activity team or Fund Team
steps.system: Event brief, capital activity workbook and FA-01 event calendar
steps.description: Use client instructions and bank records to confirm entity, deal, amount, expected or received cash and requested payment date. Determine distribution-only versus combined call-and-distribution net event; assign a second reviewer, list tax-team needs and link the controlling FA-01 event calendar. Record the setup in the brief and workbook.

steps.title: Is event context sufficient?
steps.description: Consider received-cash deal context and conflicting client instructions. The route for expected cash without conflicting instructions is UNKNOWN.

steps.title: Escalate unclear event
steps.description: Escalate received cash without deal context or conflicting instructions. The client identifies and classifies it in writing before modeling; retain confirmation with bank support.

steps.title: Identify and classify proceeds
steps.description: Confirm expected versus cleared cash and match it to portfolio company, deal, fund and bank account. Classify each component as return of capital, realized gain, dividend or income, or another supported category; flag asset conversion, escrow, holdback and other economics-changing pieces. Record in the proceeds-input tab with bank support and client correspondence alongside. Do not determine deal, tax or GAAP classification from the bank description alone.

steps.title: Are proceeds supported and tied?
steps.description: Check that classified proceeds equal the modeled amount and every component has support. Bank information alone may not establish the deal or character.

steps.title: Obtain client classification
steps.description: Stop calculations and obtain written client classification when bank activity alone does not establish the deal or character.

steps.title: Update cumulative proceeds
steps.system: Prior approved cumulative proceeds working file, system power report and accounting files
steps.description: Add current proceeds by supported classification to the prior approved file. Confirm prior distributions, remaining invested capital and cumulative contributions. Reconcile starting and current balances to the prior event, general ledger, trial balance, bank records and partner-capital records. Pull the system power report, trial balance and partner-capital files for historical balances. The second reviewer verifies the work; timing relative to advancement is UNKNOWN.

steps.title: Are balance differences addressed?
steps.description: Every difference must be resolved or documented for a reconciled waterfall starting point. An unexplained starting-point difference pauses the calculation until cleared.

steps.title: Wait for balance clearance
steps.description: The waterfall calculation does not start until an unexplained starting-point difference is cleared. Clearance owner and exact resumption point are UNKNOWN.

steps.title: Confirm waterfall rules
steps.actor: Event preparer and second reviewer, with client input
steps.description: Use the LPA, side letters, approved model, prior treatment and event facts. Record order and definitions for return of capital, preferred return, catch-up, carried interest, residual split and any holdback or clawback. Confirm fund, deal, tranche or other calculation segment and escrow or holdback treatment.

steps.title: Are waterfall rules clear?
steps.description: Determine whether the rule set is traceable to governing documents and independently reviewed, or whether changed treatment or an ambiguous LPA rule requires written direction.

steps.title: Obtain written rule direction
steps.actor: Event preparer; client or legal adviser
steps.description: Record changed treatment or ambiguity, pause and obtain written direction from the client or legal adviser. The team does not invent a missing rule.

steps.title: Lock event rule set
steps.description: Lock the event rule set when traceability and independent review are established, or after written interpretation returns.

steps.title: Run cash waterfall
steps.description: Enter current proceeds and apply return of capital, preferred return, catch-up, carried interest and residual calculations in approved order. Calculate LP and GP allocations, including holdback. Check allocated plus retained or held cash equals modeled proceeds and agrees with locked rules. Investigate negative, residual or otherwise unexpected results.

steps.title: Investigate unexpected waterfall
steps.description: Investigate a negative, residual or otherwise unexpected result. Where economics are unclear, obtain client or legal confirmation before going further.

steps.title: Is the fund in carry?
steps.description: If the model shows a carry position, include cash carry allowed by the waterfall; otherwise no cash carry is paid.

steps.title: Document and confirm carry
steps.description: The preparer documents what the model shows and the reviewer confirms it, whether or not the fund is in carry.

steps.title: Obtain and assess tax allocation
steps.actor: Event preparer; client's tax team or tax adviser
steps.description: Obtain the event taxable-income allocation from the client's tax team or adviser, who provide or approve tax conclusions. Add conclusions to the calculation, recognize taxable income may differ from cash, and assess whether the GP or another investor receives taxable income without corresponding cash. Do not substitute a GPFS-derived tax conclusion.

steps.title: Hold for tax input
steps.description: Hold final economics while required tax input is missing or conflicting. Do not replace the approved tax conclusion with one worked out by the team.

steps.title: Is tax distribution permitted?
steps.description: For taxable income without cash carry, the client's tax adviser or client decides whether a tax distribution is permitted or required. The participant refers to governing-document permission. The route when this condition does not arise is UNKNOWN.

steps.title: Calculate tax distribution
steps.system: Dedicated section of capital activity workbook
steps.description: If governing documents permit it, calculate or add the tax distribution needed to cover tax liability. Keep support separate from cash waterfall support.

steps.title: Carry tax allocation forward
steps.description: If a tax distribution is not permitted, carry the approved taxable-income allocation forward without a tax distribution.

steps.title: Approve tax inputs and output
steps.actor: Client's tax team or client; event preparer obtains approval
steps.description: The preparer obtains the tax team's or client's approval of tax inputs and output before withholding. Approval evidence and rejection handling are UNKNOWN.

steps.title: Calculate and review withholding
steps.description: Using client or tax-team schedule and direction, identify affected investors, jurisdictions and rates. Apply the approved rate to the approved taxable-income base or bring in the approved client schedule as supplied. Include approved prior-period true-ups or supplemental adjustments separately. Calculate gross, withholding and net cash per investor; check gross less withholding equals net and totals reconcile to the model and approved tax input. The second reviewer checks the result. A late or revised schedule or missing detail is escalated.

steps.title: Is this a net event?
steps.description: Distribution-only events have no netting and net cash is gross less withholding. Net events include approved withholding in the call-and-distribution net calculation.

steps.title: Calculate and confirm netting
steps.description: Include approved withholding in the call-and-distribution net calculation and keep separate support for each component before netting. The reviewer or client confirms the netting.

steps.title: Is withholding input approved?
steps.description: Proceed to investor allocations if withholding input is in and approved. A late or revised schedule, or missing rate, jurisdiction or investor classification, requires escalation and affected work is held or recalculated.

steps.title: Escalate withholding input issue
steps.description: Escalate to the client or tax adviser if the schedule is late or revised or a rate, jurisdiction or investor classification is missing. Affected calculations, notices and payments are held or recalculated until a new schedule version and renewed approval are available.

steps.title: Calculate investor allocations
steps.system: Capital activity workbook allocation engine and final summary tab
steps.description: Confirm the governing allocation basis, potentially commitment percentage, LP percentage, deal-specific basis or another basis. Use the approved investor list and approved special allocations. Calculate investor proceeds components, carry and tax effects, withholding and net cash; reconcile totals to the fund-level waterfall and tax schedules. Populate the final summary tab, later used for notices and payment support. Amounts are draft.

steps.title: Do investor allocations reconcile?
steps.description: Check investor totals equal approved fund-level components subject only to documented rounding. An unexplained difference or percentage unsupported by the governing method pauses work. Excel percentages alone are not authoritative.

steps.title: Wait for allocation resolution
steps.description: Pause for an unexplained allocation difference or unsupported percentage until resolved. Resolution owner and resumption point are UNKNOWN.

steps.title: Review distribution package
steps.system: Working files and draft notices; comment location UNKNOWN
steps.description: Review proceeds, waterfall, tax, withholding, allocation and notice-support working files and draft notices. Check proceeds amount and classification, continuity from the prior event, waterfall rules and formulas, carry, preferred return, tax distribution and holdbacks; compare tax and withholding inputs with approved schedules; check investor totals, gross, withholding, net and reconciliations; check notice labels, GAAP and tax breakdowns and footnotes. Record comments; each must be resolved. Sign off when cleared before anything goes to the client.

steps.title: Correct review issues
steps.actor: Event preparer, client or tax adviser, as applicable
steps.description: Return unresolved errors or source gaps to the preparer, or to the client or tax adviser for their input. Work stops until issues are fixed and the reviewer clears them.

steps.title: Seek client approval
steps.description: Send the internally cleared package to the client, identifying every estimated, pending or late tax input that may move. The preparer coordinates and the client approves. If changes are requested, incorporate approved changes, recalculate affected amounts and repeat reconciliations and review checks before seeking final written approval again.

steps.title: Lock approved version
steps.description: After final written client approval, lock and retain the version used for notices, posting and payment. Nothing is released or paid from an unapproved version; written approval must be on file before any entry or payment.

steps.title: Produce and reconcile notices
steps.system: Controlled Word notice template and locked investor schedule
steps.description: Mail-merge investor data from the locked approved schedule into the controlled Word template to produce PDFs. Each notice discloses gross proceeds, components, transaction type, taxable income, withholding, net payment and applicable footnotes. The preparer and reviewer reconcile every notice to the locked schedule and complete QA.

steps.title: Hand over execution support
steps.description: In the same notice-production step, hand approved posting and payment support to the Fund Team and Treasury. Execution proceeds through FA-01 and FA-17; individual gate details are UNKNOWN.

steps.title: Are release gates complete?
steps.description: Payment and notice release go ahead if notice and payment totals agree to the locked schedule and all FA-01 and FA-17 gates are complete. Notice mismatch, bank closure, invalid instructions or incomplete approval holds affected work. Investor Services holds release for a notice that does not match the approved investor list; Treasury holds payments for incomplete approvals, instructions or funding, or a holiday or cut-off.

steps.title: Hold affected release or payment
steps.actor: Investor Services or Treasury, as applicable
steps.description: Investor Services holds notice release when a notice does not match the approved investor list. Treasury holds payments for incomplete approvals, instructions or funding, or a holiday or cut-off. The participant also reports holds for notice mismatch, bank closure, invalid instructions or incomplete approval. Resolution and resumption are UNKNOWN.

steps.title: Send distribution wires
steps.description: Treasury sends the wires. Written client approval must be on file before payment; payment and notice release require notice and payment totals to agree to the locked schedule and all FA-01 and FA-17 gates to be complete. The relative order of posting, wires and notice publication is UNKNOWN.

steps.title: Resolve threatened wire timing
steps.description: If a bank holiday or cut-off threatens wires, the client and Treasury decide between changing timing and an approved alternative execution plan. Keep the revised calendar and approval. Its exact position relative to a Treasury hold and resumption mechanics are UNKNOWN.

steps.title: Follow controlled correction process
steps.description: If a change arrives after an entry is recorded or payment made, follow the controlled correction process and obtain renewed approval. Internal steps and resumption point are UNKNOWN.

steps.title: Update post-distribution records
steps.actor: Assigned Fund Team or event preparer
steps.system: Investor capital accounts, historical records and cumulative proceeds and carry tracking
steps.description: After money goes out, track tax withholding separately from investor net payments and give supporting records to whoever pays the tax authority. Update investor capital accounts, historical contributions and distributions, cumulative proceeds history and carried-interest tracking. Client-specific uploads or open-template reporting are also completed in the post-distribution step; their exact order relative to reconciliation is UNKNOWN.

steps.title: Does final distribution reconcile?
steps.actor: Assigned Fund Team or event preparer
steps.description: Reconcile actual wires, withholding held or remitted, general ledger balances and the locked schedule. Gross distribution must equal net investor cash plus withholding; actual cash and accounting must agree to the locked event without unexplained difference. If remittance ownership is unclear, a responsible role must be assigned before closeout.

steps.title: Escalate closeout exception
steps.actor: Assigned Fund Team or event preparer
steps.description: Immediately escalate unremitted withholding, a rejected wire or an accounting difference and keep closeout open. An unexplained difference prevents closeout and may require correction or reposting. Recipient and recovery mechanics are UNKNOWN.

steps.title: Close reconciled event
steps.actor: Assigned Fund Team or event preparer
steps.description: Close the event when final reconciliation is satisfied, subject to assigning a remittance role if ownership was unclear. Keep the reconciled post-distribution record and remittance support. Retention location is UNKNOWN.

steps.title: Record general ledger entry
steps.description: The Fund Team records the general ledger entry. Written client approval must be on file before any entry is recorded. No order relative to wires or notice publication is established.

steps.title: Publish investor notices
steps.description: Investor Services publishes notices on the investor portal. Release requires notice and payment totals to agree to the locked schedule and all FA-01 and FA-17 gates to be complete. Investor Services holds release when a notice does not match the approved investor list.

steps.title: Complete One Rock Cobalt upload
steps.actor: Assigned Fund Team or event preparer
steps.description: For One Rock, complete the client-specific Cobalt upload within two days of the event. This is reported in post-distribution work; its exact sequence relative to reconciliation and closeout is UNKNOWN.

topics.answer: The intake calls the work Distribution Economics: Waterfall, Tax Withholding & Notices. The participant describes setup, economics, notices and post-distribution closeout. Other team names and the parent-process boundary are UNKNOWN.

The work produces approved distribution economics and investor notices, supports posting and payment, and reconciles the event. The participant did not explicitly describe the overall delivered value or all downstream consumers.

Received or expected proceeds, a deal close or realization, or a client request can start an event. It is event-driven without a fixed calendar. The detector, notification method and event-specific fixed deadlines are UNKNOWN.

Closeout requires gross to equal net investor cash plus withholding and actual cash and accounting to agree with the locked event without unexplained differences. The reconciled record and remittance support are kept, and an unclear remittance role must be assigned. Remittance proof, retention location and downstream consumer are UNKNOWN.
UNKNOWN. The preparer, second reviewer, client, Fund Team, Treasury and Investor Services perform or approve distinct actions, but overall accountability was not identified.

The preparer briefs and classifies the event, rolls proceeds forward, confirms and locks rules, calculates the waterfall, incorporates client tax conclusions, applies withholding and investor allocations, and sends a reconciled package for second review. After written client approval and locking, final notices and execution support are produced; Fund Team, Treasury and Investor Services perform their reported actions. Post-payment records and final reconciliation support closeout. Missing inputs, reconciliation issues, review comments, timing and payment exceptions can pause or return work; several recovery points and handoffs remain UNKNOWN.

The preparer ties classified proceeds, waterfall cash, withholding and allocations; the second reviewer verifies the roll-forward and reviews the package, records comments and signs off before client submission. Tax inputs and output need client or tax-team approval, and final written client approval precedes locking, entries and payments. Notice/payment totals and all FA-01/FA-17 gates govern payment and release; final reconciliation governs closeout. Some failure recovery, retained-evidence locations, thresholds, segregation and system enforcement remain UNKNOWN.

Distribution-only events have no netting; net events include approved withholding in the call-and-distribution net calculation with separate component support and reviewer or client confirmation. Tax-distribution treatment depends on the client or adviser decision and reported governing-document permission. One Rock requires a Cobalt upload within two days. Reasons, boundary tests, effort, charging and removal constraints are UNKNOWN.
UNKNOWN. The participant described holds, recalculation and escalation, but did not identify which work is painful or estimate its effort.

Incomplete inputs hold economics, notices or payments; holidays and cut-offs can threaten wires; rejected wires, unremitted withholding or accounting differences keep closeout open. Broader financial or client consequences were not described.

Reported materials include the event brief, workbook, prior approved proceeds file, LPA, side letters, approved waterfall model, methodology record, approved tax and withholding schedules, controlled Word notice template and FA-01/FA-17 references. No documents were supplied or reviewed; locations and availability are UNKNOWN.

The account explicitly discusses fund, deal and investor-level economics and a One Rock reporting requirement. Other entity applicability, parent lifecycle, whether this is general GPFS or client-specific practice, and the basis for any standard are UNKNOWN.

The preparer and reviewer use the LPA, side letters, approved model, prior treatment and event facts to record waterfall order and scope. Changed or ambiguous treatment is referred to the client or legal adviser in writing. The client or tax adviser decides tax-distribution treatment; tax conclusions and withholding schedules come from the client side. The model calculates waterfall allocations and the workbook calculates investor amounts. Detailed calculation dimensions, dates, rounding beyond documented allocation rounding, source conflicts and interpretation records remain UNKNOWN. Mentioned documents were not reviewed.

The process consumes client deal, tax and withholding information and prior accounting records. It hands approved posting and payment support to Fund Team and Treasury; Investor Services publishes notices; tax-payment support goes to the person responsible for payment, whose identity is UNKNOWN. FA-01 and FA-17 are used for execution; detailed gates, notice handoff, other dependencies and counterpart confirmation remain UNKNOWN.

The event brief and capital activity workbook hold setup and calculation work; the waterfall model, methodology record, system power report and accounting files support calculations and reconciliation. A Word mail merge produces PDF notices; Investor Services uses an investor portal and the One Rock upload uses Cobalt. Storage, authoritative records, workbook logic ownership and most transfer methods are UNKNOWN.
